custom-box-structure-guide.title: Custom Box Structures: Lift-Off, Magnetic, Drawer or Carton?
custom-box-structure-guide.seoTitle: Custom Box Structures: Lift-Off, Magnetic, Drawer or Carton? | MTT Packaging
custom-box-structure-guide.summary: Compare custom box opening styles for perfume, skincare and gift sets. Separate rigid, folding and corrugated structures before choosing materials and artwork.
custom-box-structure-guide.intro: Choose the opening around the product and how the buyer will use it. A removable lid, hinged cover and sliding tray create different handling needs; none alone establishes protection or quality.
sections: Start with the product, not the decoration

Write down the assembled product dimensions, filled weight, number of pieces, sales channel and intended opening sequence. Distinguish internal box size from the outer size used to plan a bag or shipper. A screen image is useful for visual direction, but does not establish dimensions or closing clearances. Select the structure first so that artwork follows the real panels and seams.
Lift-off versus magnetic: what changes for a bottle?

A lift-off rigid box has a separate cap and base. It exposes the contents when the cap is removed, but the user needs somewhere to put the lid. A magnetic book box keeps its lid attached at the spine and needs room for that lid to swing. Both require a bottle support and clearance over the cap. Choose the handling experience before choosing the finish. Compare the single-bottle lift-off design with the hinged skincare set layout; the latter illustrates a different product arrangement, not an interchangeable bottle insert.
Drawer, hexagonal and pillow are different structural decisions

A drawer tray moves inside a sleeve: review the pull attachment and product retention while it slides. A hexagonal lift-off box has matching six-sided components and needs a deliberate internal layout. A pillow carton closes at curved ends and offers a different usable volume from a rectangular tray. Compare the coffee drawer, hexagonal sweets box and pillow carton. These are selection references, not proof of a tested load or finished order.
Keep the packaging families clear

Wrapped rigid board is one construction family; creased paperboard cartons and fluted corrugated packs are others. A corrugated mailer may also have a rear-hinged lid, but its folded walls and side wings are not the same construction as a wrapped magnetic book box. Use the family comparison to separate presentation and transport requirements. The FEFCO design catalogue provides a common naming reference for corrugated styles; a style code does not specify board performance.
Approve opening and removal before print production

Load the sample with the actual contents. Remove the lid, slide the drawer or open the flap repeatedly as the customer would. Check the tall parts of the product, finger access, seam alignment and any ribbon pull. Then review artwork at the folds and wrap joins. Avoid assigning one clearance to every design: material thickness, dimensions and construction affect the fit.
Send two options for a useful comparison

Shortlist two structures with the same contents and quantity. Ask for the board, wrap, insert, print, finishes, setup charges and shipping scope to be identified separately. A comparison with different inserts or delivery terms is not a like-for-like price comparison. Send your product measurements and preferred opening, or use the box planning tool for an initial visual brief.
faq: Is a magnetic box always more luxurious than a lift-off box?
No. Material feel, finish execution, fit and the intended opening experience matter. Compare physical samples for the same product rather than ranking quality by the closure alone.
Can a rigid box ship flat?

Some purpose-designed collapsible rigid boxes can fold flat. A conventional assembled lift-off box does not. Confirm the actual supplied configuration and the assembly required at your packing location.
Does a hinged lid make a mailer a rigid gift box?
No. A corrugated mailer uses fluted board and folded locking parts. A wrapped rigid book box uses a different board and assembly method even though both can open from the rear.

rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.title: Rigid Box vs Folding Carton vs Corrugated: How to Choose
rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.seoTitle: Rigid Box vs Folding Carton vs Corrugated: How to Choose | MTT Packaging
rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.summary: Compare rigid boxes, folding cartons and corrugated packaging by presentation, packing, material use and shipping needs, with practical product examples.
rigid-box-vs-folding-carton.intro: Use rigid boxes for the presentation experience you want, folding cartons for an appropriate retail format, and corrugated packaging for an assessed transport or mailer role. A project may need more than one layer.
sections: Three families, three different starting points

• Rigid box: structural board is wrapped or otherwise finished and assembled into a firm presentation format. Some designs are collapsible; many are supplied erected.
  • Folding carton: creased paperboard forms panels, end flaps and glued or locking features. Supply and erection methods depend on the design.
  • Corrugated packaging: fluted material between liners forms shipping cartons, mailers or other structures. Board grade, joints, supports and the route must be reviewed together.
Paper thickness alone is not a complete performance specification.
Choose by what the customer must do

A gift recipient may keep a rigid box; a retail customer may open a carton once; a fulfilment team needs a pack that can be assembled and sealed consistently. Start with those tasks. A magnetic skincare set presents several items together. A crash-lock skincare carton provides a different retail packing route. A four-flap corrugated carton can serve an outer transport role. They are not interchangeable specifications.
Compare total scope, not a presumed cheapest family

Request a quote for the same product count, quantity and delivery scope. Separate board and wrap, insert, printing, finishing, tooling, assembly and packing. Also ask for sample charges and freight. Do not assume a universal quantity at which one family becomes cheaper: size, production route, print coverage and setup all matter. Obtain packed carton dimensions if empty packaging must travel to your filling site.
Premium appearance is not limited to one board family

A folding carton can use precise typography, bright printing and an appropriate finish. A rigid box can be restrained or colourful. Neither a magnet nor a drawer is sufficient to define quality, and similar opening actions can be engineered in different materials. Evaluate the actual construction and sample rather than relying only on names such as “luxury” or “premium”.
Separate the display box from shipping protection

For a perfume order, compare a presentation box with a corrugated mailer. If one sits inside the other, size the outer pack from the finished packed presentation box. Agree product restraint, sealing and an appropriate testing plan. A beautiful box, a flute designation or a style drawing does not establish that the full pack will survive the distribution route.
A short selection checklist

• What is the complete product envelope and loaded weight?
  • Is the pack for display, carrying, delivery or several of these?
  • Will it arrive at the filling site flat or erected?
  • Who assembles, loads and seals it?
  • Are inserts, cards and a bag part of the order?
  • Which physical sample and transport checks need approval?
Request a comparison using the same brief. For opening details, read the box structure guide.
faq: Are all rigid boxes unable to fold flat?
No. Collapsible rigid structures exist. Specify whether your chosen design is supplied assembled or flat, and include assembly work when comparing costs.
Does a folding carton need an outer shipping pack?
That depends on the product and distribution route. Do not assume a retail carton alone is adequate for parcel shipping; review the full loaded system.
Which family is the cheapest?
There is no dependable universal ranking for every project. Compare quotes with the same contents, quantities, finishes, packing and delivery scope.

custom-inserts-product-protection.title: Paperboard vs Molded Pulp vs EVA: Choosing Custom Inserts
custom-inserts-product-protection.seoTitle: Paperboard vs Molded Pulp vs EVA: Choosing Custom Inserts | MTT Packaging
custom-inserts-product-protection.summary: Choose a custom insert around product geometry, removal access and packaging use. Compare paperboard, molded pulp, EVA and fabric-covered support.
custom-inserts-product-protection.intro: The best insert is the one that supports your actual product and lets the customer remove it comfortably. Choose the material after defining the contents, box opening and distribution conditions.
sections: Measure the assembled product and identify contact areas

Provide dimensions with caps, pumps and decorations fitted, plus filled weight and photographs from several sides. Mark surfaces that should not be rubbed or loaded. Define whether the product lies down or stands up. A jar and two bottles, as in the skincare set, need separate positions and a review of lid clearance. Do not size a cavity from a photograph or nominal bottle capacity.
Paperboard: folded support with deliberate contact points

Folded or die-cut paperboard can create platforms, dividers and locating features. Specify where the product rests and how it is restrained; an attractive empty cutout does not prove support. Review creases, assembly and loaded deformation on the sample. Check the full material combination and local collection route before making recyclability claims. The carton example uses paperboard support, with grade and fit still to be confirmed.
Molded pulp: formed geometry and a tooling decision

Molded-fibre inserts can form three-dimensional support around a product. Surface appearance and dimensional behaviour depend on the process and material. Confirm the tooling scope, sample method and product contact areas before selecting it for appearance alone. Read the molded-pulp guide for cosmetics alongside your actual product requirements.
EVA and covered support: specify the full build

Cut foam can form locating cavities, but foam type, density, thickness and the remaining material between cavities need review. A fabric cover changes the contact surface and usable fit. Check for rubbing, lint, adhesive visibility and removal force. In the ring keepsake layout, the fabric-lined slit must suit the ring and its setting; the lining is not automatically an anti-tarnish material.
Access can matter as much as a tight fit

Allow a practical grip, finger recess or secured lift ribbon. A cavity that holds an item but makes removal awkward is not finished engineering. For a drawer, check stability during sliding; for a hinged lid, check the closing sweep; for a lift-off lid, check the full height under the cap. Use the opening guide to coordinate the insert and box.
Validate the full pack and record the approved version

Use actual contents to check loading, removal, closure and the intended handling sequence. Confirm the transport test scope for the complete pack separately. Record material, cavity drawing, product revision and approved sample together. If the bottle or cap changes, review the fit again. Send the product data for an insert review; include quantity, destination and any direct-contact requirements.
faq: Is EVA always the safest insert for glass?
No material name establishes protection on its own. Geometry, support, material properties and the complete shipping pack need a loaded-sample review and appropriate testing.
Can one insert hold a whole gift set?
Yes, if each item has suitable support and removal access. Include every item, leaflet and accessory when defining the available space.
Is a paper insert automatically recyclable?
Do not assume that. Review coatings, adhesives, combined materials, separation and the actual collection route in the destination market.

how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.title: Custom Packaging Brief Checklist: What to Send for a Quote
how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.seoTitle: Custom Packaging Brief Checklist: What to Send for a Quote | MTT Packaging
how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.summary: Prepare a packaging brief with dimensions, quantity, materials, artwork, inserts and delivery scope. Includes a copyable checklist for boxes, bags and gift sets.
how-to-write-a-packaging-brief.intro: A useful brief states what is known and marks what is undecided. You can request guidance before final artwork is ready, but a production quote needs a reviewed specification and clear delivery scope.
sections: Describe the product as it will be packed

Measure the actual assembled product, including caps and projecting parts, and provide its loaded weight. List the number of pieces in each set. For food already sealed in a tray or pouch, measure that sealed pack rather than the loose contents. For example, the macaron window carton must accommodate the tray rim and cover as well as the food.
Use the right dimension convention

State finished internal box dimensions as length × width × height, and label product dimensions separately. A shopping bag uses width × side gusset × height and should be sized from the finished outer box with an agreed loading orientation. Do not reuse the bottle dimensions as bag dimensions. Identify the unit of measurement and mark all provisional dimensions.
Copy this enquiry checklist

• Product name and current development stage:
  • Assembled product dimensions, units and loaded weight:
  • Items per set and individual sizes:
  • Packaging role: retail / gifting / parcel delivery:
  • Preferred structure or two options to compare:
  • Material and finish preferences, or undecided:
  • Insert, bag, card, ribbon and tissue requirements:
  • Quantity by size, artwork version and accessory:
  • Artwork files and separate foil / UV / emboss artwork, if ready:
  • Destination, target arrival date and delivery terms to discuss:
  • Optional budget range and currency:
  • Sample, tooling and testing requirements:
Mark missing items “to be confirmed” instead of guessing.
Ask for an itemized commercial scope

Separate the box, insert and accessories, and ask which print and finishing operations are included. Request sample and tooling costs separately, plus freight and any tax or duty assumptions. State whether packing takes place at your facility or elsewhere. A price for an empty box and a price for a packed gift set cover different work. Use the coffee set to consider whether tasting cards are supplied loose or placed in the box.
Food and sensitive product details need their own review

State whether packaging touches the food directly, the storage conditions and the destination. A general “food grade” label is not enough to determine suitability for a particular use. The FDA explains how food-contact component status is assessed for the United States; other destinations need their own review. This guide does not certify any catalogue pack.
Keep one current specification and a clear approval path

Attach the current artwork revision and identify who approves structure, colour and the physical sample. Do not approve print files while the structure is still changing. Start with the box planning tool if a visual draft helps, or send the checklist directly. Neither an account nor a completed tool design is required to enquire.
faq: Can I ask for a quote before I know the material?
Yes. Share the product, quantity, opening preference and delivery needs, and mark the material undecided. A final price still needs an agreed specification.
Can a reference image replace dimensions?
No. It communicates appearance and opening direction, but it does not establish the actual product envelope or manufacturing dimensions.
Should bags and ribbons use the same order quantity as boxes?
State quantities separately. Extra bags, multiple ribbon lengths or different artwork versions may change the required quantities and quote.

printing-finishing-guide.title: Matte, Gloss, Foil or Spot UV: Custom Packaging Finishes
printing-finishing-guide.seoTitle: Matte, Gloss, Foil or Spot UV: Custom Packaging Finishes | MTT Packaging
printing-finishing-guide.summary: Compare matte and gloss surfaces, foil, embossing and spot UV for custom packaging. Learn what to specify and check on the actual paper sample.
printing-finishing-guide.intro: Choose the effect you need the customer to see or feel, then test that finish on the intended substrate. A finish name alone does not predict its appearance on every paper or cloth.
sections: Matte versus gloss: start with the broad surface

A matte surface gives a less reflective appearance; a gloss surface emphasizes reflections and printed colour. Coatings and film laminations are different specifications and should not be treated as interchangeable. Compare the gloss perfume design with the matte collagen set as visual directions, then approve physical paper samples. A screen cannot reproduce surface feel.
Foil adds a surface effect, not an opening structure

Foil can highlight a logo or outline, but the result depends on the foil, paper, tooling and production route. Keep delicate detail away from difficult wrap corners and discuss the artwork with the converter. The hexagonal gift design combines dyed paper and gold foil outlines. The cloth-wrapped ring design needs its own foil trial because cloth texture differs from smooth paper.
Emboss and deboss change surface relief

Embossing raises a feature; debossing presses it into the surface. Artwork, tooling, material thickness and assembly sequence affect the result. Ask how the effect is made in the chosen build and whether it affects the reverse surface. A border on the textured skincare wrap should be evaluated on that material rather than copied from a smooth-paper proof.
Spot UV needs a defined area and a compatibility check

Selective gloss UV can contrast with a matte background. Supply a separate mask for the intended area and agree alignment requirements with production. Review adhesion, cure, fold behaviour and the visual result on the selected surface. Do not assume the same gloss on absorbent uncoated stock and coated paper. The collagen set is a reference for this surface contrast.
Match a set with physical references

A rigid-box wrap, bag paper and greeting card can show the same ink differently. Decide whether the priority is the closest colour match, the same texture or a deliberate contrast. Compare the assembled set under consistent lighting and retain the approved reference. Review ribbons and foil alongside the printed paper rather than choosing each from unrelated screen images.
Prepare artwork and quote each operation

Identify ordinary print, foil, UV and relief areas separately. Keep key information away from cuts, folds and wrap joins using the allowances agreed for that structure; there is no single safe-zone value for all packaging. Ask for each setup or tooling charge and sample scope. Send your artwork and preferred finish, using the brief checklist if the specification is still open.
faq: Can I combine foil, embossing and spot UV?
A combination may be feasible, but the substrate, operation sequence, detail and registration need review. Specify the intended areas and ask for a sample before committing to production.
Will a gloss finish make any material look the same?
No. The base material, printed coverage and coating or lamination route affect appearance. Compare the actual materials.
Does more finishing always mean better packaging?
No. Choose effects that support the design and remain clear in production. Several competing effects can make the hierarchy less readable and add setup costs.

packaging-design-to-production-china.title: Packaging Design to Production in China: Boxes, Bags & Gift Sets
packaging-design-to-production-china.seoTitle: Packaging Design to Production in China: Boxes, Bags & Gift Sets | MTT Packaging
packaging-design-to-production-china.summary: Coordinate box structure, inserts, bags, cards and artwork from brief to physical sample and production approval, with a clear specification for each component.
packaging-design-to-production-china.intro: A coordinated packaging set needs more than matching artwork: each box, insert, bag and card needs an agreed size, material and approval reference. Keep one project brief with separate component specifications.
sections: Plan the full set before finalising the box

List what is supplied: presentation box, product insert, paper bag, ribbon, card, tissue and any shipping carton. State the quantity for each component and whether it arrives loose or assembled. The hexagonal gift box and paper bag example illustrate different component choices; they are not a dimensionally matched set. A pictured accessory is not automatically included in a quotation.
Use the finished outer box to size the bag

Confirm the box’s external dimensions after wrapping and assembly, its loading orientation and the total carried weight. Specify bag width × side gusset × height. Test insertion, removal and handle attachment with the complete set, including tissue. A loose ribbon and a structurally secured lift ribbon have different functions and should be identified separately.
Approve colour across the materials, then freeze revisions

The same artwork on box wrap, bag stock and card paper can differ in colour and sheen. Approve them together and record each substrate and finish. When a box size changes, recheck the bag, insert, card placement and shipping carton before release. The finish guide explains the physical references to request; use the enquiry checklist to keep commercial scope aligned.
faq: Can MTT review a box, bag and card in one brief?
Yes. List each component, its quantity and how the set is packed. Dimensions, material options and sample approval still need to be confirmed for every component.
Does matching artwork guarantee the same colour on every component?
No. Paper, texture and surface finish affect reproduction. Approve the components together against physical references.
What should happen if the product or box size changes?
Recheck the insert, finished outer size, bag fit, card placement and shipping pack. Keep the revised specification linked to the approved artwork and sample.
